target_customer: Consumers wanting wireless multi room audio from existing speakers (original product); later IoT sensor buyers
problem: Existing speakers could not stream music over wifi without buying expensive new systems.
business_model: Hardware sale of a 99 to 149 dollar dial, later cloud connected sensors
product_category: Consumer audio hardware, then IoT sensors

founders.name: Daniel Conrad
founders.background_notes: One directory says he was an early product manager on other products; not from an opened source.

competitors.name: Sonos
competitors.traction_then: Speakers started at 199 dollars each; Beep pitched itself as the cheaper option

technical_complexity.rationale: Custom wifi audio hardware with firmware, caching and decoding in the device and streaming service integrations.

defensibility.rationale: A design patent was filed February 2014, but Chromecast style adapters and Sonos could compete on price and features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source on direct incumbent action; the company stopped making the device.

market_need_then: Reviewers in 2014 framed it as Chromecast for audio and a low cost Sonos alternative for existing speakers.

brand_strength.rationale: Press in February and December 2014 covered the dial, but many unrelated brands use the word beep and no community evidence was found.

pivots.to: Long range low power IoT sensors and network
pivots.why: A podcast summary says the CEO chose to stop making a connected device and find a new model; the YC page now describes ten year battery sensors.

outcome_analysis: Beep launched a 99 dollar audio dial in 2014, raised several seed amounts and shipped Spotify support, then abandoned the device and pivoted to IoT sensors. Dealroom lists it as closed without a date. The pivot did not find a lasting position, but no post-mortem confirms the cause.
notes: Funding conflict: CB Insights totals 5.02M over 5 rounds, while the recorded rounds sum to 5.72M; the 4M round is dated 2014-11-01 by StartupIntros and 2014-12-01 by Hypebot and may overlap another round. The 1.6M June round is from the Hypebot text and not independently confirmed. Website returned HTTP 522. Daniel Conrad is named by the YC page; the search tool flagged a possible reconstruction on another site. Founder education not found. Pivot failure is inferred from the podcast summary and inactive status.
